Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

DATA WE NEED FROM YOU (four items behind logins or paywalls):
1. The PACER docket for the U.S. government's antitrust case against Apple in the District of New Jersey — scheduling order, trial date, discovery cut-offs and the remedy sought. It dates the largest structural threat.
2. The latest annual accounts of Apple's three Irish entities (Apple Operations International, Apple Operations Limited, Apple Distribution International) from the Irish Companies Registration Office — entity-level profit and IP ownership, which set the durability of the 15.6% effective tax rate.
3. A USPTO Patent Center or Espacenet export of Apple patent families filed 2024–2026 in on-device AI, wearable health sensing, foldable displays and AR/VR optics; Apple discloses no patent count, so the IP moat is unquantified.
4. The CFO prepared remarks from Apple's 2026-07-30 earnings call: the 47–48% September gross-margin guide and its 1-point refund component were stated on the call, not in the release, so without the transcript that guide is trade-reported rather than verified.

FURTHER DILIGENCE: the December-quarter gross margin ex-refund; the terms of the first renewal of the search payment; the annual report's refund and inventory split; China revenue against its nine-month base; and Services growth after the U.S. link-out injunction.

Version 2 — the version the committee approved — is delivered, with the HTML report, its PDF and the sources in the delivery folder. Version 3 was an unreviewed copy saved afterwards and was not released.

RATING: Watchlist, composite 5.7/10. No position at $344.63 (2026-10-30 close); a 1–2% starter at $240–265, a 3–4% full position at or below $225, capped at 4%; 12–24 month horizon.

THESIS: Apple's franchise is as strong as the market believes — more than 2.5bn active devices, a 76.3% services gross margin, $136.7bn trailing free cash flow — but the price capitalises a margin peak, not a floor: June's 50.1% gross margin included 2.0 points of tariff refunds and the September guide is 47–48%. On margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at the 30.2x five-year average multiple, fair value is $268 and probability-weighted value $266, 22–23% below the close; Apple is investable below $265.

MAIN RISKS: gross margin settling near 45% as memory costs rise and the lower-cost inventory cushion ends (fair value $205–257); a de-rating to the 21x peer median ($186, 46% below); the ~$20bn Google search payment, 22% of services gross profit and ~9.4% of market value, held on one-year non-exclusive terms with argument from 2026-12-09; China lapping a +30% nine-month base while Huawei leads; App Store commissions, tariff re-escalation after 2027-01-10, and a buyback running at 39.5x.

ONE QUESTION: Is Apple's ~50% gross margin a new floor, or a tariff-refund and memory-timing peak? The 2026-11-02 December guide answers it: at or above 48% ex-refund the base case moves toward $296, near 45% it converges on the $205 bear.

TAKEAWAYS: (1) zero position today — probability-weighted value $266, a 23% negative return despite the franchise; (2) buy $240–265 for 1–2% and at or below $225 for 3–4%, capped at 4% because one regulatory event is worth 9.4% of market value; (3) the 2026-11-02 guide decides the case, with 2026-12-09 and 2027-01-10 as the next dated tests.

Research only, not investment advice.
